title: The Great
summary: Ashoka Maurya was an Indian emperor of the Maurya Dynasty, who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from c. 268 to 232 BCE. A convert to Buddhism after witnessing the Kalinga War, Ashoka propagated Buddhist teachings and promoted social welfare throughout his vast empire.

events.title: Birth of Ashoka
events.description: Ashoka was born to Emperor Bindusara and Subhadrangi in Pataliputra, making him a member of the Maurya dynasty. Details of his early life are limited, but he was likely trained in martial arts and statecraft.

events.title: Ashoka appointed as Governor of Ujjain
events.description: During his father Bindusara's reign, Ashoka was appointed as the governor of Ujjain. His role was to maintain order, administer justice, and oversee the province's economic activities, demonstrating his administrative abilities early on.

events.title: Ascension to the Mauryan throne
events.description: Following the death of his father, Bindusara, Ashoka ascended to the Mauryan throne. Accounts suggest there was a struggle for succession before he successfully secured his position as emperor.

events.title: The Kalinga War
events.description: Ashoka waged a devastating war against the kingdom of Kalinga. The immense suffering and loss of life witnessed during the war deeply affected him, leading to his conversion to Buddhism.

events.title: Ashoka's conversion to Buddhism
events.description: Deeply remorseful after witnessing the Kalinga War's devastation, Ashoka embraced Buddhism. Inspired by the teachings of peace and non-violence, he vowed to rule with dharma (righteousness).

events.title: Implementation of Dharma
events.description: Ashoka implemented a policy of Dharma across his empire. He established hospitals for humans and animals, built roads and rest houses, and promoted religious tolerance. Officials called Dharma Mahamatras were appointed to spread the Dharma.

events.title: Erection of Pillars of Ashoka
events.description: Ashoka erected pillars throughout his empire inscribed with his edicts. These pillars served as a means to disseminate his message about dharma, good governance, and social responsibility, reaching a wide audience.

events.title: Dispatch of Buddhist Missionaries
events.place: Across the Mauryan Empire and beyond
events.description: Ashoka actively promoted the spread of Buddhism by dispatching missionaries to various kingdoms. His son Mahindra and daughter Sangamitra were sent to Sri Lanka and these initiatives helped introduce Buddhism in Central Asia and Southeast Asia.

events.title: Ashoka's Death
events.description: Ashoka died in Pataliputra after a long and influential reign. His death marked a turning point for the Mauryan Empire, which began to decline shortly afterward.
